description:
Several sibling tool calls in one script, through the in-process `probe-tool` fixture.

`probe-tool delay` answers after 100 ms, `fail` at once with status 7. The oracle has no such
tool, so every case here is a fixture: what bash would do given a command with that behaviour.

cases.name: siblings: concurrent calls keep their own statuses
cases.script: probe-tool delay >/tmp/d & a=$!; probe-tool fail 2>/tmp/f & b=$!; wait $a; echo a=$?; wait $b; echo b=$?; cat /tmp/d /tmp/f

stdout.text:
a=0
b=7
completed:peer=false
named fixture error

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: siblings: wait -n reports the first call to finish
cases.script: probe-tool delay >/dev/null & probe-tool fail 2>/dev/null & wait -n; echo first=$?; wait; echo all=$?

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command

cases.name: siblings: kill cancels one pending call and the other completes
cases.script: probe-tool delay >/tmp/k & k=$!; probe-tool delay >/tmp/o & o=$!; kill $k; wait $k; echo killed=$?; wait $o; echo other=$?; cat /tmp/o; cat /tmp/k 2>/dev/null; echo end

expected.reason: probe-tool is a fixture of the cooperative example; the oracle has no such command
